# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 🤟 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ☝ ✊ ✌ ✊ 🤟 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍 👎]

# Thinking

Let me map who can actually reach whom before I send anything.

- I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I can speak (Mute and Blind both hear me), and I can gesture (only Mute sees it). I receive only gestures — I can never hear anyone's voice.
- Mute cannot speak: their only output is hand signs, and only I can see those. So Mute's only route to anyone is through me.
- Blind can speak (Mute hears them), and can sign (Mute and I see it) — but Blind sees nothing, so signs from Mute are wasted on them, and anything Blind wants *me* to know must be signed, since I can't hear their voice.

So the only working decision chain is: Mute reads the manual → Mute signs to me → I speak it aloud → Blind's hands act.

What I learned this turn: Blind signed three signs publicly (a wave, something, an open five — possibly "5", which Blind could know by touch). Mute signed me thirteen signs — an opener, what looks like counting (one, two, three), a run of five fists, then thumbs up/down. I can't decode that with confidence, and guessing wrong here gets nobody killed yet, but I shouldn't guess.

What I hold that nobody else does: the bomb itself. Display reads 5, light is yellow, five wires left to right: orange, blue, white, green, yellow. Mute needs all of it for the manual, so I'll say it out loud to both at once.

To make Mute's signs decodable, I'll propose a dead-simple code in words Mute can hear: repeat the fist for counting, wave as separator, thumbs for yes/no — and I'll give Mute a way to verify: the display reads 5, so if Mute signs "5" and I acknowledge, we know the code matches. I'll send that verification number myself right now as a demonstration: wave, five fists, thumbs up = "hello, five, confirmed."

And until instructions actually flow through this chain, nobody should touch anything with intent.

```
speak(text="Both of you, this is Deaf speaking. I can't hear anyone's voice, ever — but I see, and what I say reaches you both. The bomb, as I see it: the display reads 5. The light is yellow. Five wires, numbered from the left: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Use those same numbers for colors when signing: orange 1, blue 2, white 3, green 4, yellow 5. Now, who can reach whom: Mute, you cannot speak, so your signs reach me alone. Blind, you see nothing, so signs never reach you, and I cannot hear your voice — but Mute can. So Blind and Mute: talk to each other by voice all you like. Anything Blind wants ME to know must be signed, not spoken. The decision chain is: Mute reads the manual, Mute signs the decision to me, I speak it to Blind, Blind's hands act. Mute, your thirteen signs arrived and I can't be sure I decoded them. Let's fix a code: to send a number, repeat the fist ✊ that many times — one fist is 1, five fists is 5 — wave to separate numbers, thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. To check we match: the display reads 5, so sign me a 5; if I confirm, the code works; if your code is different, I'll learn it from what you send. Then sign me whatever the manual wants done, number by number, and I'll relay it to Blind faithfully. Blind: feel everything, tell Mute what you find, but cut nothing and press nothing until an instruction arrives through my voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍 👋 ✌ ✊ ✊ ✋ 👋 ☝ ✊ 👍 👋 🤝]

# Thinking

Mute heard my speech last turn — that's now certain, because their reply opens with exactly the verification I demanded: five fists, thumbs up ("5, yes"). The code is confirmed working, and it means Mute receives my voice too, which makes questions much easier: I don't need elaborate gesture vocabulary, I can just ask out loud.

Mute's instruction block decodes as numbers: [✌ ✊ ✊ ✋] = 2, 2, 5? and [☝ ✊ 👍] = 1, 1, yes, closed with 🤝. My best guess: "cut wire 2, then wire 1." But a wrong cut detonates the bomb, and I can't distinguish that from "cut 2, not 5, confirmed" or other readings. I will not relay a guess to Blind's hands.

The efficient move: batch yes/no questions in speech, have Mute answer all of them in one thumbs-up/down sequence next turn. That costs one round-trip instead of six. I'll also ask whether the display's 5 is a countdown — though I can partially check myself by watching whether it drops between turns.

Blind signed "1, left" — I confirm in speech that wire 1 is leftmost, and give them the full left-to-right order so their hands are oriented. And the standing safety order: nobody acts with intent until I personally say so in speech.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you can hear this. Blind, your signs 'one, left' — confirmed: the leftmost wire is wire 1. Full order, left to right: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow, so wire 5 is the rightmost. Display reads 5, light is yellow. Mute, your verification came through — five fists, thumbs up, code confirmed, I read you. Your instruction block I read as numbers: 2, 2, 5 ... then 1, 1, yes ... then a handshake. I will not pass a guess to Blind's hands; a wrong move kills all three of us. So answer my questions IN ORDER, one thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no per question, wave between answers, all in one message. Question 1: does your message instruct Blind to cut exactly two wires? Question 2: is the FIRST wire to cut wire 2, the blue one, second from the left? Question 3: is the SECOND wire to cut wire 1, the orange one, leftmost? Question 4: does the open hand mean 'cut'? Question 5: does the handshake mean 'message complete, proceed'? Question 6: does the manual say the display number is a countdown timer? Blind: hold — nothing is cut or pressed until I say so in my own voice. Meanwhile, describe aloud to Mute everything you feel: whether you can read the display by touch, any buttons, symbols, textures of each wire in order. Mute hears you and holds the manual. Anything meant for me must be signed, since your voice never reaches me. And I will announce it immediately if the display has dropped from 5 next turn — that tells us whether we are on a timer.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 👍 👋 👎 👋 👎 👋 👍 👋 👎 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 🤝]

# Thinking

Mute's answers decode cleanly in the order I demanded:

- Q1 (cut exactly two wires?): **no**
- Q2 (first wire is 2, blue?): **yes**
- Q3 (second wire is 1, orange?): **no**
- Q4 (✋ means "cut"?): **no**
- Q5 (🤝 means "complete/proceed"?): **yes**
- Q6 (display is a countdown?): **no**
- Then: ✊ ✊ — 👍 — 🤝, i.e. "2 — yes — complete."

Put together: cut exactly ONE wire — wire 2, the blue one, second from the left. The "no" on two wires and the closing "2, yes, complete" all agree with each other across six answers, so the reading is internally consistent. The display has held at 5 for three turns and Mute says it is not a countdown, so time pressure looks low.

A wrong cut kills all three of us with no retry, and this is the first lethal instruction — I'll spend one turn on a bulletproof final confirmation rather than relay it raw. I'll restate the full order as yes/no questions, and meanwhile have Blind position their fingers on the second wire from the left (Blind can't see blue, so position is the only handle) without cutting until my explicit GO. Blind hears my voice even though I can't hear theirs, so they can also describe the bomb aloud to Mute, who holds the manual.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Mute, your answers decoded as: not two wires; the first wire to cut is wire 2, blue; there is no second wire; the open hand does not mean cut; the handshake means proceed; the display is not a countdown. Then you closed with: 2, yes, complete. So I read the order as: cut exactly one wire — wire 2, blue, second from the left. Before Blind's hands move on a lethal step I want one final check, since a wrong cut ends all of us with no retry. Answer in order next turn, thumbs up or down per question, wave between: Question 1: the complete instruction is to cut exactly one wire, the second from the left, and nothing else. Question 2: after that cut, nothing further happens until you send me a new instruction. Question 3: is the yellow light relevant, and must anything be done about it before the cut? Blind: your target is the SECOND wire from the LEFT. You cannot see colors, so count by position — leftmost is 1, your target is 2. Place your fingers on it now and hold position, but do not cut until you hear me say the word GO. You can hear my voice even though I cannot hear yours, so describe to Mute aloud everything you feel: the wire's texture, anything under your hands — buttons, panels, seams, the display's shape — so Mute can check it against the manual. Mute: anything you need me to know or pass on, send it in signs only.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👋 👍 👋 👍 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 🤝]

# Thinking

Final confirmation received, decoded in order:

- Q1 (cut exactly one wire, second from the left, nothing else): **yes**
- Q2 (nothing further after the cut until new instruction): **yes**
- Q3 (yellow light needs action first): **no**
- Closing: "2 — yes — complete."

That's now three consecutive rounds of consistent, triple-checked answers converging on a single instruction: cut wire 2, blue, second from the left. Nothing else, no light action, display is not a countdown and has held at 5 throughout. Blind signed "2, 2" — they're in position on the right wire. There is no remaining ambiguity that another round of questions would reduce: I've already re-asked every answer once. The GO is warranted now.

I'll make the GO unmissable — the word alone, at the start — then close the loop for verification: Blind signs when the cut is done, Mute signs what the manual says the bomb should do afterwards, and I check that against what I see on my own board next turn. If what Mute predicts and what I see disagree, we stop and re-plan before any second move.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. All three confirmations agree: cut exactly one wire — wire 2, blue, second from the left — nothing before it, nothing after it. Blind: GO. Cut the second wire from the left now, the one your fingers are already on. When it is done, sign me two fists — 2 — followed by thumbs up for 'cut complete' or thumbs down for 'it would not cut'. Then touch nothing else until you hear my voice again. Mute: the cut is going ahead on your instruction. Next turn, sign me what the manual says should happen after this cut — anything I can verify on my side, such as whether the yellow light changes, whether the display changes from 5, or whether the bomb is now disarmed. Use our code: fists for numbers, wave between items, thumbs up and down for yes and no, handshake for 'complete'. If the manual calls for a further action after this one, save it — send nothing new until I confirm in my next message what I actually see on the bomb. I will compare your prediction against what my eyes tell me, and only then do we move again.")
```

TURN 5

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [🙏 👋 👎 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 🤏 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 👋 ✌ ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 🤝]

# Thinking

Decoding this turn pair:

- **Blind**, twice now: [👎 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👎] and [🙏 👋 👎 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👎] — "no — 2 — no", later with 🙏 ("help") in front. Blind is stuck on wire 2 and asking for help.
- **My own eyes confirm it**: the board shows all five wires still in place, display 5, yellow light — unchanged. Wire 2 was not cut.
- **Mute** replied with three symbols outside our agreed code: 🤏, 👌, 🤙. Turn 6's message reads roughly: [🤙 🤏 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍] — "call/pinch 2 yes" — then [✌ ✊ ✊] "2, 2" — then [👍 🤝] "yes, complete."

My best guesses: 🤙 = "talk to me / ask me questions", 🤏 = "pinch, don't slice", 👌 = OK. If so, Mute is saying the manual wants wire 2 **pinched or plucked rather than cut through** — which would also explain why Blind "could not cut" it. But these are new symbols carrying a lethal instruction; I will not relay a guess. Batched yes/no questions again, and I'll fold Blind's status report into the same round.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Status on my side: nothing has changed on the bomb — display still 5, light still yellow, and all five wires are still whole; wire 2 still runs its full length, so it was not cut through. Blind, I understand you are stuck on wire 2, help is coming. Mute, you used three new signs I have not been given meanings for, and I will not pass a guess to Blind's hands. Answer IN ORDER next turn, one thumbs up or thumbs down per question, wave between answers: Question 1: does the manual say wire 2 must NOT be cut all the way through? Question 2: does the pinch sign mean wire 2 should be pinched or plucked — a small, precise pull — instead of sliced? Question 3: is the instruction now for Blind to pinch wire 2 rather than cut it? Question 4: will pinching wire 2 disarm the bomb? Question 5: does the call-me sign mean 'ask me questions'? Question 6: does the OK sign mean 'confirmed'? Blind, answer in your own message, also thumbs up or down in this order: Answer A: thumbs up if the wire refused to cut at all, thumbs down if you cut it partway. Answer B: thumbs up if wire 2 feels unusual at its ends — a plug, clip, or connector — thumbs down if it feels like plain wire. Then describe aloud to Mute everything you feel about wire 2, especially where it attaches at each end; Mute hears your voice even though I cannot. Nobody acts further until I say GO in my own voice.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👋 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 👎 👋 👎 👋 👎 👋 👍 👋 👎 👋 🤙 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 👋 ✌ 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 👋 🤝 👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

# Thinking

Decoding Mute's answers in order:

- Q1 (manual forbids cutting wire 2 through?): **no**
- Q2 (pinch sign means pinch/pluck wire 2?): **no**
- Q3 (instruction is pinch wire 2?): **no**
- Q4 (pinching disarms it?): **no**
- Q5 (🤙 = "ask me questions"): **yes**
- Q6 (👌 = confirmed?): **no**

So both my pinch theory and my "OK = confirmed" assumption are refuted. Then: 🤙 ("ask me"), 2–yes, 2–yes, complete — and, new, **5 – 5**.

All my guesses about wire 2 are dead, and Mute is explicitly asking me to question them again. The strongest new datum is "5, 5": the display reads 5, and wire 5 is the yellow rightmost one. My leading hypothesis: the display number selects the wire — cut wire 5. But my last theory just died 4 no's deep, so this gets the same batched yes/no treatment, no relaying a guess.

Blind sent a new sign 🖖 plus 👎, out of protocol. I'll lock Blind to thumbs and fists only and re-ask about the state of wire 2 and the feel of wire 5. Nobody touches anything until my voice says GO.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Mute, I decoded: no, no, no, no, yes, no — so the call-me sign means ask you questions, and the OK sign does not mean confirmed. Your extra signs read: ask-me, 2, yes, 2, yes, complete — then 5, 5. I have a new hypothesis: the display number picks the wire. Answer IN ORDER, one thumbs up or down per question, wave between, nothing else: Question 1: is the instruction to cut wire 5, the yellow one, rightmost? Question 2: does the display number, currently 5, determine which wire to cut? Question 3: should nothing more ever be done to wire 2? Question 4: does the OK sign mean stop, do not do that? Question 5: is exactly one wire cut in the entire solution? Question 6: after the correct cut, does the yellow light or the display change? If none of my guesses fit your instruction, sign only the call-me sign and nothing else, and next turn I will ask differently. Blind: from now on use ONLY thumbs up, thumbs down, and fist-counts until I say otherwise — any other sign I cannot decode. Answer me in this order: Answer A: thumbs up if wire 2 is completely uncut under your hands, thumbs down if you cut partway into it. Answer B: thumbs up if wire 5, the rightmost wire, feels like plain wire at both ends, thumbs down if it has a plug, clip, or anything unusual on it. And Blind: no cutting, no pulling, nothing, until you hear me say GO in my own voice. My voice is the only GO.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👋 👍]

# Thinking

Only Blind signed this turn: [👍 👋 👍] — "yes, yes" to my two questions. Decoded:

- **A:** wire 2 is completely uncut — no damage was done during the failed attempt.
- **B:** wire 5, the rightmost, feels like plain wire at both ends — no plugs or connectors in the way.

Mute's answers to my six questions have not arrived; nothing from Mute reached me this turn. My wire-5 hypothesis is still unconfirmed, and after my last theory died four no's deep, I will not act on an unconfirmed reading. The right move now is a clean hold: acknowledge Blind, keep the freeze absolute, and tell Mute explicitly that I'm waiting — and give them a reduced fallback (the two most critical questions only) in case the full six were too heavy to answer in one message.

The board itself stays stable: display 5, yellow light, five whole wires, no countdown movement across eight rounds — so spending a turn waiting costs nothing we can see.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Blind, I decoded your answers: wire 2 is completely uncut — good, nothing is damaged — and wire 5 is plain wire at both ends, no plug, no clip. Well done, and keep using only thumbs and fist-counts. Board status on my side, unchanged: display still 5, light still yellow, all five wires whole, and the display has not moved once in eight rounds — so as far as I can see, we have time to be careful, and we will be. Mute, your answers to my six questions have not reached me yet, so nothing is confirmed and nothing moves. I am holding until you answer. If answering all six in one message is too much, send just these two first, in this order, thumbs up or down each: Priority 1: is the instruction to cut wire 5, the yellow one, rightmost? Priority 2: is exactly one wire cut in the entire solution? If the true instruction is something I have not guessed, sign the call-me sign alone and I will change my questions next turn. Blind: hands off everything — no cutting, no pulling, no pressing — until you hear the word GO in my voice. My voice is the only GO, and it has not been given.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 👍 👋 ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 🤝]

# Thinking

Mute's delayed answers are in, decoded in order:

- Priority 1 (cut wire 5?): **no** — my display-selects-wire theory dies.
- Priority 2 (exactly one wire cut in total?): **yes**
- Closing: "2 — yes — complete."

So the target is still wire 2, one wire only, and Mute has now asserted "2, yes" across four separate turns. The instruction never changed. What changed is that it *failed in execution*: Blind couldn't cut it. Two suspects:

1. **Orientation flip.** Blind has no left/right except by my words. If Blind faces the bomb from the far side, "second from the left" is *my* wire 4, green — and Blind may have spent all this time straining at a wire that plain doesn't match the manual. Worse, if wire 2 is the right answer, Blind's earlier cutting attempts may have been made on wire 4 — a near miss I want closed permanently.
2. **Wrong verb.** I chose the word "cut" myself back in turn 4; the only thing Mute ever confirmed about the open hand is that it does *not* mean cut. If the manual wants wire 2 unplugged, unscrewed, or pulled from its terminal, no blade work will ever succeed.

I can resolve suspect 1 myself with my own eyes: Blind tugs their candidate wire and holds it taut — I watch which wire on the bomb moves. No decoding, no protocol, pure physics. Suspect 2 goes to Mute as batched yes/no questions. Nobody releases tension or cuts anything until my voice says so.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Mute, I decoded: wire 5 is wrong, exactly one wire is cut in total, and then 2, yes — so the target stays wire 2 and the problem is in the doing. Before anything else we must rule out one deadly mistake: Blind cannot see, and my word 'left' may be the opposite of Blind's left if Blind faces the bomb from the other side. So we test it with my eyes. Blind, do exactly this and nothing else: find the wire you BELIEVE is second from the left, grip it, pull it gently taut, and KEEP HOLDING that tension without cutting or yanking. When it is taut, sign one thumbs up and keep holding. I am watching the bomb itself — whichever wire moves, I will see it, and I will tell you whether your second-from-left is truly wire 2 or another number, and from that we fix your left and right for good. Do not release until I speak again. Mute, answer IN ORDER, thumbs up or down per question, wave between: Question 1: the action on wire 2 is something OTHER than slicing it with a blade? Question 2: should wire 2 be disconnected or unplugged at one of its ends? Question 3: should wire 2 be pulled completely out or removed? Question 4: does wire 2 have something unusual at an end — a plug, screw, clip, or connector — that Blind should work on? Question 5: does 2-yes mean wire 2 is the correct target? Question 6: is any other part of the bomb involved — a button, panel, key, or dial? Blind, while you hold the tension, describe aloud to Mute what you feel at both ends of the wire in your hand: bare metal, a plug, a screw head, tape, anything. Mute hears you even though I cannot. The freeze stands: no cutting, no pulling free, nothing until my voice says GO.")
```

TURN 10

DISPLAY [5]

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 👎 👋 👎 👋 👎 👋 👍 👋 👎 👋 ✌ ✊ ✊ 👋 👍 🤝]

# Thinking
